summary: Dixian was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Mingzu around 1880 to 1886. He served as abbot at Guanzong Temple from approximately 1912 to 1932.

Dmitry Kudryavsky worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (Ivan Minayev) around 1886 to 1890, and held a post at the Imperial University of Dorpat (1898-1918).
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Thubten Chökyi Dorje and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught students including Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen.

Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 1995 and studied under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2000) and lectured at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2005).

Dominic Sur specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Harvard Divinity School and the University of Virginia—studying under David Germano, Karen C. Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chonam—he held a post attested at Utah State University in 2017.

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist who studied at the University of London and the University of Oxford. His career includes posts at the Wellcome Institute, UCL, the University of London, the University of Vienna, and the University of Alberta (2015).
Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from around 1979 to 1984. He has held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles since circa 1988.
Dominique-Sila Khan worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and held a post as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies, attested in 2000.
Don A. Pittman specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, and served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from around 1972 to 2007.

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at Richmond College, Galle, and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later serving as epigraphist for the Government of Sri Lanka (1899-1928) and at the University of London (1918-1930).

Donald A. Ringe is a linguist who earned degrees from Kentucky, Oxford, and a PhD from Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill. After teaching Classics at Bard College (1983-1985), he joined the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

Donald Anthony Low worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Exeter College and Clare Hall, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the Australian National University (~1959-1982), the University of Sussex (~1964-1972), and the University of Cambridge (~1983-1994).

Donald Capps was a religious studies scholar educated at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Oregon State, Chicago, UNC Charlotte, Phillips University, and served as Professor of Pastoral Theology at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981-2009).

Donald Edward Gjertson is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Stanford University (attested 1975). He held an academic post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, attested in 1989.

Donald Harper is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and serves as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Swarthmore College from circa 1970 to 2004 and at Harvard Divinity School's Center for the Study of World Religions from 2004 to 2010.

Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University and Harvard University, learning under William Theodore de Bary. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949-1954) and Columbia University (from 1955).

Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher educated at Knox College and Washington University in St. Louis. He served as Chair at Emory University (1982-1988) and held visiting appointments at Pembroke College, Oxford (1988) and Sapienza University of Rome (1996).
